title: Kundalini climbs to meet Shiva
hook: the sleeper wakes and climbs, lotus by lotus, to a meeting at the crown
carry: at the crown, shakti and shiva are one
tomorrow: why would a map of the body have letters on its petals?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the chakras as a map, and a week of maps that share one word: wheels, circles, made to be traveled. Today, the traveler sets out.

An elevator in a tall building chimes at every floor, and every time the doors slide open on a different hallway. The old map has a journey like that, only slower. The serpent who slept across the door at the base of the spine has lifted her head. The road is open. And she begins to rise, one lotus at a time, each one turning toward her as she passes, toward a place at the very top that she has never reached.
screen: `A CHIME AT EVERY FLOOR.` → `THE SLEEPER LIFTS HER HEAD.` → `SHE RISES, ONE LOTUS AT A TIME.`

segments.voice: The Sat-Cakra-Nirupana tells the climb center by center. She passes the root, the lotuses above it, the heart with its unstruck sound, the throat, the place between the brows. Each station has its own shape and sound, and the meditator follows her with attention, stop by stop. Then, above them all, at the crown, the text sets a lotus of a thousand petals: Sahasrara. That's where she's going. And when she arrives, she isn't alone. There, the text says, kundalini, Shakti, the Goddess as power, unites with Shiva. So the top of the map isn't a light switching on. It's a meeting. And under the meeting sits one of tantra's biggest teachings: Shakti and Shiva are never truly two. Shiva is pure awareness; Shakti is the power that moves, and everything that moves is her. The climb is that power coming home to its own source. It's why Hindu homes and temples so often show Shiva and Parvati side by side, and sometimes as one figure, Ardhanarishvara, half him and half her. The Sri Yantra's point held the same two as one. A thousand petals inside the skull? The text isn't asking that. Some readers take the thousand as fullness, more than anyone could count. And the story isn't finished at the summit. The text has one more page, and it comes later in the run.
screen: `THE CLIMB, LOTUS BY LOTUS.` · `SAHASRARA: A THOUSAND PETALS.` · `NOT A SWITCH: A MEETING.` · `SHAKTI AND SHIVA, NEVER TWO.` · then, large: `AT THE TOP, A MEETING.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and rest your attention at the base of your spine. With each slow breath, let it climb a little: the belly, the heart, the throat, the brow, the crown. At the top, don't reach for anything; stay there, and let it be a meeting rather than a finish line.
The chakras as a map: a climb, lotus by lotus, to Sahasrara, the thousand-petaled crown, where Shakti and Shiva meet.
screen: `THE CHAKRAS AS A MAP — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: at the crown, Shakti and Shiva are one. The power comes home to its source. Day sixteen forty-six, climbed.

howItsDone: In kundalini meditation as the tantric texts describe it, practitioners move attention upward center by center toward the crown, usually under a teacher's guidance.

chat.meaning: In the Sat-Cakra-Nirupana kundalini, Shakti, climbs to the crown and unites with Shiva; in tantra the two are one reality, power and awareness.

Shiva.meaning: the god whom Shakti meets at the crown

Ardhanarishvara.meaning: Shiva as half woman: Shiva and Parvati in one body
